VERDICT.headline: best net-of-fee Sharpe = 2.7 (95% CI [-0.77, 6.08], 3-fold 1/3, at MAKER fee 0.5 bps/side on LIQUID5, short-only q=top100% min-hold K=30 bars=90min), turnover 29.6 /day -- BUT CI straddles 0 and it is a DIRECTIONAL/beta artifact, NOT tradable residual alpha.

beta_drift_diagnostic.interpretation: long-only loses while short-only gains by ~symmetric magnitude => the positive net is DIRECTIONAL down-drift in the test window, not cross-sectional residual alpha. A real alpha would make long and short roughly symmetric.

VERDICT.verdict_paragraph: Brutally honest: on the y180 HF180R residual signal, the tail-magnitude + min-hold + reversal-exit family does NOT produce a robustly tradable net-of-fee strategy. Across the full 6-book x 5-tail x 4-K x 3-fee x 2-universe sweep (480 configs), NOT A SINGLE config has a day-block bootstrap 95% Sharpe CI that excludes zero. The single highest net Sharpe is 2.7 (LIQUID5 short-only, top-band, K=30/90min, 0.5bps maker) but its CI is [-0.77,6.08] (straddles 0), it is only 1/3-fold positive, and it is exposed as a directional/beta artifact: long-only loses ~-26 bps/day gross while short-only gains ~+40 bps/day gross, i.e. the PnL is the market down-drift in the OOS window, not residual alpha. The genuinely alpha-isolating L/S tail books are uniformly negative net at every fee >=0.5bps (gross edge ~0.0006-0.16 bps/step is annihilated by turnover). The best 3/3-fold config (LIQUID5 short-only q30 K30) makes +40 bps/day @0.5bps but collapses to 1/3 at 1bps and goes negative at 2bps, with fold0 carrying essentially all the PnL. Tail-magnitude filtering helps gross/turnover ratio (raises breakeven fee from ~0.06 to ~0.20-0.35) but never enough to clear realistic maker fees with statistical significance. CONCLUSION: this strategy family is fee-fragile and CI-straddles-0; the only profitable corner is unhedged short directional drift, which is not a deliverable alpha. Net tradable Sharpe with significance = effectively 0.
